 Widespread, heavy rain to kick off November 
 By Shawn Cable Published : Oct. 31, 2026 at 9:40 AM CDT | Updated : Oct. 31, 2026 at 9:44 AM CDT Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google A significant soaking rain is looking more and more likely Monday, Tuesday and even lingering into Wednesday. Rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches or more will be possible across much of Minnesota and northern Iowa. 
 This system will have a tremendous amount of moisture to work with for early November. Rain will begin developing Sunday night, then become widespread Monday as a strong, slow-moving area of low pressure moves into the Upper Midwest. Monday looks like the wettest day, with moderate to heavy rain at times.
 Rain will continue Monday night into Tuesday as the low slowly moves across Minnesota. A few showers could even linger into Wednesday before the system finally pulls away.
 A widespread 1 to 2 inches of rain looks increasingly likely, with a band of 2 to 3 inches or more possible. Right now, the potential for some of the highest totals has shifted into western and central Minnesota. Southern Minnesota and northern Iowa will also see a good soaking, although amounts will depend on the exact track of the low.
 KEYC Weather (KEYC Weather) We’re still a couple of days away, so the exact placement of the heaviest rain will probably move around some. We’ll get a much better idea of the track, timing and rainfall amounts as we move through the weekend.
 Keep your KEYC First Alert Weather app handy. The weather team will continue to track the system and have the latest updates as everything develops.
